A 51% attack is not really a threat for many reasons. The big thing about Bitcoin is that it's decentralized and so all actions taken are publicly visible. If somebody is exploited this computational tier to start doing things like double spending or juking transactions and the like, it would be completely transparent.

So what would happen? A fork would quite rapidly emerge, with a new form of work (or a new style of proof - such as proof of stake), and it would become the new standard. What this really means is that even if somebody does gain 51% of the power, it would completely insane and illogical for them to do anything except keep Bitcoin as healthy as possible. Exploiting their position would not only destroy it, but gain them little. It likely would not even destroy Bitcoin, if that was their goal.

If someone ever pulled off a 51% attack, it would be over and done before anyone knew about it. They would simply rewrite a blockchain in a way that puts the BTC in their control, and cash out (most likely into another crypto) in the time it took for a handful of verifications to go through. After that no exchange would ever touch the currency again.

Sure bitcoin would persist, and the other half of the fork would still exist, but it would nuke the value. That sort of risk is completely unacceptable in my book, but if losing 95% of value in an afternoon doesn't scare you off, then more power to you. I remain skeptical.
